definition: The EXtensible Cross-Linguistic Automatic Information Machine (EXCLAIM) was an integrated tool for cross-language information retrieval (CLIR), created at the University of California, Santa Cruz in early 2006, with some support for more than a dozen languages.
details: The lead developers were Justin Nuger and Jesse Saba Kirchner. Early work on CLIR depended on manually constructed parallel corpora for each pair of languages. This method is labor-intensive compared to parallel corpora created automatically. A more efficient way of finding data to train a CLIR system is to use matching pages on the web which are written in different languages. EXCLAIM capitalizes on the idea of latent parallel corpora on the web by automating the alignment of such corpora in various domains. The most significant of these is Wikipedia itself, which includes articles in 250 languages. The role of EXCLAIM is to use semantics and linguistic analytic tools to align the information in these Wikipedias so that they can be treated as parallel corpora. EXCLAIM is also extensible to incorporate information from many other sources, such as the Chinese Community Health Resource Center (CCHRC). One of the main goals of the EXCLAIM project is to provide the kind of computational tools and CLIR tools for minority languages and endangered languages which are often available only for powerful or prosperous majority languages.

explainer.lead: EXCLAIM is a tool for building training material for cross-language information retrieval, where someone searches in one language and finds information in another. Created at the University of California, Santa Cruz in early 2006 by lead developers Justin Nuger and Jesse Saba Kirchner, it reduces the need to build parallel corpora by hand.

tiers.eli5: Imagine finding two copies of the same story in different languages and matching their parts so a computer can learn how the languages correspond. EXCLAIM looks for such matching material on the web, especially across different-language Wikipedias. This can help people search in a familiar language and still discover information written in another.
tiers.practitioner: EXCLAIM automates the alignment of latent parallel corpora on the web, using semantic and linguistic analysis to turn matching multilingual pages into CLIR training data. Wikipedia is a major source, while its extensible design also allows sources such as the Chinese Community Health Resource Center. It replaces some labor-intensive, language-pair-specific corpus construction, but the approach depends on suitable matching pages being available.
tiers.paperLevel: Given documents in different languages, EXCLAIM identifies and aligns latent parallel web corpora using semantics and linguistic analytic tools, producing material that can train a cross-language information retrieval system. This addresses the cost of manually constructing parallel corpora for every language pair and supports extensibility across domains and sources. A central project goal is to make CLIR tools available for minority and endangered languages, not only prosperous majority languages.

explainer.example: Suppose English and Chinese Wikipedia contain matching articles about diabetes. EXCLAIM aligns their information using semantic and linguistic analysis, creating a parallel corpus that can help train a CLIR system to respond to an English query with relevant Chinese-language information.

explainer.intuition: The web already contains pages in different languages that describe the same things, forming a hidden or latent parallel corpus. EXCLAIM finds and aligns this material automatically so it can teach a retrieval system how information connects across languages.
howItWorks: Collect matching web pages written in different languages.
Use Wikipedia's multilingual articles as a major source of comparable material.
Apply semantic and linguistic analysis to align the information.
Treat the aligned material as parallel corpora for training CLIR systems.
Extend the process with other sources, such as the Chinese Community Health Resource Center.
explainer.whyItMatters: Automatically aligning existing web material is less labor-intensive than manually constructing a parallel corpus for every language pair. It also offers a route to retrieval tools for minority and endangered languages that often lack the resources available for majority languages.
misconceptions: It is not just a bilingual dictionary; it aligns multilingual material to support retrieval.
It is not restricted to Wikipedia; its extensible design allows additional sources.
It is not focused only on major languages; minority and endangered languages are a central goal.
